transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. Can you start by telling me what brings you in to see me today?

Well… I’m here because I feel like I’ve been pushed into having to explain something that everybody keeps acting like is just me misunderstanding it, but I’m not. For about a year now I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously that parts of my dad’s lab results—his chart, the numbers, the way they show up in the clinic system—something is being changed or held back.

I know how that sounds, and I know people keep telling me, “The results are fine,” or “You’re reading too much into it,” but I work in healthcare, I’m a phlebotomist, so I’m not just some person randomly looking at a screen and making things up. I know what I saw, and what’s in the chart now doesn’t match it. And it’s not just one little typo or something that could be explained away. It feels like someone in the clinic system is deliberately keeping certain parts from showing, or altering how they appear.

My family is tired of hearing about it, the doctors keep brushing it off, and honestly I’m worn down from trying to prove it. But I can’t just let it go when it’s my dad’s health and the records don’t match what I saw. That’s why I’m here.
Aside from your concerns about the lab results, have you ever heard voices or sounds that others couldn't hear, or seen things that weren't really there?

No, I mean… not like voices talking to me or anything like that. I don’t hear someone telling me things, and I don’t see people who aren’t there, if that’s what you mean.

I know why you’re asking, because once I start explaining the lab result situation people jump to that, like, “Is she hearing things?” or “Is she seeing things?” But that’s not what’s happening. This is about records and numbers and what showed up versus what later didn’t show up. It’s not a voice in my head or some shadow in the room. I’m looking at actual information and trying to explain that it doesn’t match.

Over this past year, have you noticed any periods where your mood, energy, or need for sleep was very different from normal—like feeling unusually high, energetic, and needing much less sleep, or on the other hand feeling persistently down, low energy, and losing interest in things?

I don’t know that I’d describe it like that, no. I mean, this whole thing has been exhausting, so of course my mood isn’t exactly cheerful all the time, and I get frustrated because it feels like I’m the only one taking it seriously. But I wouldn’t say I’ve had some separate period where I was suddenly, like, unusually high or full of energy and didn’t need sleep or anything.

And on the other side, I’ve been worn down, yes, but it’s hard to separate that from the stress of what’s been going on. I still get up, I go to work, I do what I have to do. It’s not like I just stopped caring about everything for no reason. It’s more that this situation has been hanging over me, and people keep acting like the problem is my reaction instead of the records, so that gets to me.

So… no, I don’t think there have been major mood or energy swings like you’re describing. More just stress and frustration from trying to get someone to listen.

Aside from this issue with your dad's lab results, how have things been going for you generally—are you still managing your job, relationships, and daily responsibilities the way you used to, or have you noticed changes in those areas too?

Generally, I’m still functioning. I mean, that’s part of what’s frustrating, honestly, because people act like if I’m upset about this then everything in my life must be falling apart, and it’s not.

I still go to my phlebotomy shifts. I show up, I do my work, I deal with patients, I draw blood, I follow the routines I’m supposed to follow. I’m not missing bills or letting my apartment fall apart or not bathing or anything like that. I pay what I need to pay, I get groceries, I keep up with normal daily things. Maybe I’m more distracted sometimes because this is always in the back of my mind, but I’m still taking care of myself and doing what needs to be done.

Relationships are more strained around this topic, sure, because my family doesn’t want to keep hearing about it and I feel like they’re dismissing me. But outside of that, day-to-day, I’m managing. I haven’t stopped being able to live my life. I just also can’t pretend this thing with my dad’s records isn’t happening.

Aside from the situation with your dad's lab results, have you noticed yourself feeling suspicious or wary that other people—like coworkers, neighbors, or others—might be trying to deceive or harm you in some way?

Not generally, no… not like I think my neighbors are out to get me or my coworkers are plotting something against me. I don’t walk around thinking random people are trying to hurt me.

But the clinic system part, yes, that’s different. That’s why I’m here. For about a year now I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously that something is wrong with my dad’s lab results—like something was changed, or parts of it were held back, or the chart was made to look cleaner afterward than what I saw before. And I know how that sounds when I say it out loud, because people immediately make it sound like I’m accusing everyone of some huge conspiracy, but I’m not saying every person in the building is involved. I’m saying the numbers I saw and the way the records look now don’t line up.

And what wears me down is that every time I bring it up, doctors say the numbers are fine, my family says to let it go, and then it becomes about whether I’m “overreacting” instead of about the fact that the chart doesn’t match. So am I wary? In that specific situation, yes. I feel like someone in that system is not being straight with me. But outside of that, I’m not suspicious of everybody in my life.

If a trusted, independent expert reviewed the original lab data and the current chart and told you they found no evidence of any change or tampering, do you think that would change your mind at all, or would you still be certain something was altered?

I mean… I want to say yes, because I know that’s the reasonable answer, right? If someone truly independent looked at the original data and the current chart side by side, then yes, in theory that should matter to me.

But I also have to be honest: at this point I don’t think one more person telling me “it’s fine” would just erase what I saw. That’s been the problem for the past year. Everybody keeps saying the numbers are fine, the doctors say there’s nothing wrong, my family says I need to let it go, but I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw before. It isn’t just that I’m upset or confused by medical information—I work around lab results, I know how these things are supposed to look. And something about my dad’s results changed, or something was held back, or it was cleaned up afterward. That’s what I keep trying to prove.

So if the expert just said, “No evidence of tampering,” I’d want to know exactly what they reviewed, where the original data came from, whether they had access to everything, who provided it to them, whether there were audit trails—because if the information they’re given is already the altered version, then of course they’re going to say it looks fine. That wouldn’t really answer the question for me.

I’m not trying to be difficult. I know how this sounds. But I’m here because I can’t just pretend I didn’t see what I saw, and it’s wearing me down having everyone act like the issue is me instead of the records. So… no, I don’t think I would immediately change my mind. I’d listen, but I would still need proof that nothing was changed, not just another reassurance.
